title: wslua: Allow zero length TvbRanges in more cases
description:
Fix a few cases with zero length TvbRanges and Tvbs in Lua:

Allow creating a zero length Lua Tvb from a TvbRange by
calling tvb_bytes_exist instead of tvb_offset_exists.
Allow creating a zero length sub-TvbRange from a TvbRange, including
if the backing bytes are 0 length.

Add some tests for these cases.

The Lua TvbRange code does not consistently treat negative offsets
and negative lengths, and does not necessarily treat them the same
as epan/tvbuff* code. (But do we want to continue supporting negative
offsets and lengths? See #20103).

Ping #15655

notes.body:
added 3 commits
  • c5670036...f00c1dc1 - 2 commits from branch wireshark:master
  • 486f4d25 - wslua: Allow zero length TvbRanges in more cases
[Compare with previous version](/wireshark/wireshark/-/merge_requests/19070/diffs?diff_id=1269533077&start_sha=c5670036083ed26b72a060eb28fe2d695d188f9a)

Tentatively, I think that should be fixed by not allowing negative offsets, and at most only allowing len to be negative if it's -1 (or perhaps not at all), and replacing len in that case with the default value that means "to the end of the TvbRange", instead of passing it through and having it mean "to the end of the parent Tvb, which might be larger than this Tvb". For those cases that are invalid, print specific messages about how negative offsets aren't allowed.

Doing all that would then mean that `len + offset` would always be greater than or equal to `offset` and so that later test could be reduced to a single value.

@@ -23,7 +23,7 @@ local OTHER = "other"
 -- if one happens to know the number of fields and the number of values.
 --
 local n_frames = 1
-local taptests = { [FRAME]=n_frames, [OTHER]=391*n_frames }
+local taptests = { [FRAME]=n_frames, [OTHER]=394*n_frames }
 
 testlib.init(taptests)
 
@@ -908,6 +908,28 @@ function test_proto.dissector(tvbuf,pktinfo,root)
     testlib.test(OTHER, "tvbrange_offset_len_raw_offset_len", range_raw == expected,
         string.format('range_raw="%s" expected="%s"', range_raw, expected))
 
+    -- Edge cases with zero length, and different ways to create them
+    range = bytestvb1()
+    -- Subrange of a range starting with the last offset (zero length)
+    local subrange = range:range(range:len())
+    range_raw = subrange:raw()
+    expected = subrange:bytes():raw()
+    testlib.test(OTHER, "tvbrange_subrange_empty_raw", range_raw == expected,
+        string.format('range_raw="%s" expected="%s"', range_raw, expected))
+    -- Create an empty byte array (this is different because the backing
+    -- tvb is empty)
+    local emptybytestvb1 = ByteArray.new("", true):tvb("Empty bytes hex-string1")
+    range = emptybytestvb1()
+    range_raw = range:raw()
+    expected = range:bytes():raw()
+    testlib.test(OTHER, "tvbrange_empty_raw", range_raw == expected,
+        string.format('range_raw="%s" expected="%s"', range_raw, expected))
+    -- Convert the range back to an empty tvb
+    local emptybytestvb2 = range:tvb()
+    expected = emptybytestvb2:bytes():raw()
+    testlib.test(OTHER, "tvbrange_empty_tvb_raw", range_raw == expected,
+        string.format('range_raw="%s" expected="%s"', range_raw, expected))
